audit.whatIsWrong: Rated EVEN at 5.5/10 against a 37.5% win rate, while the late block itself opens 'This is where the 37.5% shows'.
audit.why: The page quotes the losing win rate in its own prose and then rates the matchup even.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every row of the level chart is wrong in both layers. It reads Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Skill / Skill / Skill; the packet chart and all seven whys read Skill / Lillia / Lillia / Lillia / Graves / Lillia / Lillia.
audit.why: whys[1] says 'she kites your first step-up' under a row saying Graves wins level 2, and whys[4] calls level 6 'your one nuke' under a row saying it's even. The chart is inverted against the text beside it at all seven stages.
audit.corrected: Both charts rewritten as one atomic group, with Collateral Damage's 100s and Lilting Lullaby's Dream Dust prerequisite written into the phase and spike text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four errors. (a) Lillia's W is called 'Blooming Blast' in six places — a name that does not exist. Her W is Watch Out! Eep!. (b) Worse, the move speed is attributed to that W; the stacking Move Speed is the PASSIVE half of Blooming Blows, her Q, gained whenever a spell hits an enemy. (c) End of the Line is said to slow her on detonation — Graves' Q has no slow at all; the only slow in his kit is Smoke Screen's impact. (d) Smoke Screen is called a blind.
audit.why: The whole lane plan was built on baiting a W that grants speed and on a Q slow that does not exist. A player following it holds his real slow (W) for zoning and tries to set up a combo off an imaginary one.
audit.corrected: Move speed correctly credited to Blooming Blows and stated as 'every spell hit', the fabricated W name removed, the slow moved to Smoke Screen's impact where it actually lives, and the blind replaced by the sight-range cut.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'True Grit armor is wasted against her magic Dream Dust DOT' and 'your True Grit armor is dead weight against percent-irrelevant magic damage'.
audit.why: Quickdraw grants an Armor AND Magic Resist boost. It is not dead weight against magic damage; it is half designed for it. The real hole is different and sharper: Blooming Blows deals extra TRUE damage on its outer edge, and true damage is what ignores both resists.
audit.corrected: Restated: the MR does help, the edge of her Q is what your resists cannot touch.
sources: enemyKit Q text and trueDamage flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'.
audit.why: Lilting Lullaby is 150 seconds at rank 1 and Swirlseed is a flat 12 — both are long enough to plan a step-up around.
audit.corrected: Swirlseed's whiff window and the R's Dream Dust prerequisite written into spikes[1] and spikes[3]; Collateral Damage's 100s into phases[4].

edits.before: Four shells of buckshot win any level-1 face-off — trade autos point-blank where every pellet lands.
edits.after: One ability each and no move-speed stacks yet — the first trade is a genuine wash, so just last-hit.

edits.before: E online — dash-reload weaving starts: auto, E for the grit armor and reset, auto again. Most champs lose this flat.
edits.after: Blooming Blows stacks her move speed on every spell hit — she kites your first step-up before Quickdraw lands.

edits.before: Full kit: Q's wall-bounce return is your real damage — fight near terrain so both hits connect.
edits.after: She bounces out of every approach and re-pokes with Swirlseed while your two shells reload.

edits.before: Trade in shell rhythm: two autos and out. Track Blooming Blows; your armor stacks from E make his short trades unprofitable.
edits.after: Quickdraw's MR does help, but the edge of Blooming Blows is true damage and her speed slips every window you make.

edits.before: Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback in one — hold it for either, never for chip.
edits.after: Collateral Damage is the one tool that outruns her kite — fire it right after a Swirlseed, on 100s.

edits.before: First item spike — the point-blank Q-AA-E-AA pattern now removes half bars. Force fights near walls.
edits.after: Your first item can't close the gap — she kites between your reloads and re-applies the DOT.

edits.before: You out-skirmish but the crit scalers pass you — convert to picks with smoke-screen blinds and R snipes.
edits.after: Lilting Lullaby sleeps you into a full combo — never face-check her, and play for picks elsewhere.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Lillia carry threat 6/10.
edits.after: Unfavoured matchup — difficulty 7/10, Lillia carry threat 7/10.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Your W smoke cuts sight range and slows on impact — drop it on the gank's arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.

edits.before: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage, E through fights for armor, and save R as either the execute or the peel knockback. Crit carries out-DPS you — picks don't care.
edits.after: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage for the slow and sight cut, E through fights for the resists, and save R as the execute. She out-kites you — picks don't care.

edits.before: Her kiting speed stacks — catch her early in the chase or not at all. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Blooming Blows stacks speed on every spell hit, so the chase is already lost — Smoke Screen's impact slow is your only pin.

edits.before: She picks up W (Blooming Blast) move speed and her Dream Dust DOT starts compounding faster than a single shell volley can answer — she kites your first step-up.
edits.after: Blooming Blows (Q) stacks her move speed every time a spell hits, and the Dream Dust DOT compounds faster than one shell volley answers — she kites your first step-up.

edits.before: True Grit armor is wasted against her magic Dream Dust DOT, and her W speed lets her slip your Quickdraw-and-shell windows through Levels 4-5.
edits.after: Quickdraw gives magic resist too, so it does blunt the DOT — but the edge of Blooming Blows is true damage and her stacked speed slips every window you make.

edits.before: Her R sleep into max Dream Dust one-shots you, and the Lvl 11/16 W upgrades make her uncatchable — she fully out-scales your point-blank range.
edits.after: Lilting Lullaby needs Dream Dust on you first, then the sleep into a full combo one-shots you — and her stacked speed makes her uncatchable at your range.

edits.before: Your only clean trade window: lay End of the Line on the wave so the detonation slows her, then Quickdraw in for a point-blank 4-shell burst before her W (Blooming Blast) gives her stacked move speed.
edits.after: Your only clean trade window: Smoke Screen her for the impact slow — End of the Line has no slow, it just detonates — then Quickdraw in for a point-blank 4-shell burst before Blooming Blows (Q) has stacked her move speed.

edits.before: Collateral Damage is your one kill button: catch her after she throws Swirlseed or mid-W-bounce and the R cone can delete her before her move-speed lets her kite out of range.
edits.after: Collateral Damage is your one kill button: Swirlseed is a flat 12 seconds, so catch her right after she throws it and the R's cone can delete her before her stacked speed kites out of range.

edits.before: Her R (Lilting Lullaby) sleeps you into a full Dream Dust + combo burst before you wake, and her Lvl 11/16 W upgrades make her uncatchable for your point-blank range — end before this.
edits.after: Her R (Lilting Lullaby) only makes you drowsy if Dream Dust is already on you, so every poke she lands is setup — then the sleep plus a full combo bursts you before you wake. End before this.

edits.after: Land Smoke Screen for the impact slow, letting Quickdraw and a point-blank shell volley connect before her stacked speed carries her out

edits.after: Use Smoke Screen to zone her off the wave and cut her sight — the impact slow is the half that matters, since nothing in her kit is auto-based

edits.before: Stack W (Blooming Blast) move speed and kite the gap while you reload your two-shell magazine so your burst never lands
edits.after: Stack Blooming Blows move speed off every spell hit and kite while you reload your two-shell magazine, so your burst never lands

edits.before: Lillia is an off-meta top pick, but she still out-ranges your point-blank shells and pokes with passive Dream Dust DOT, so the lane is annoying from minute one. Your one good window is Level 2-3: with Q and E up, drop End of the Line on the wave so the detonation slows her, then Quickdraw in for the 4-shell spread burst before her W (Blooming Blast) has any move-speed stacked. Do NOT chase past one Quickdraw charge — Blooming Blast hands her speed on every bounce and she'll kite you under tower while Dream Dust ticks. Your Smoke Screen blind is wasted on her ability-based DOT, so use the smoke to zone her off the wave instead of to fight.
edits.after: Lillia is an off-meta top pick, but she still out-ranges your point-blank shells and pokes with Dream Dust DOT, so the lane is annoying from minute one. Your one good window is Level 2-3: with Q and E up, land Smoke Screen for the impact slow — End of the Line does not slow, it only detonates — then Quickdraw in for the 4-shell burst before Blooming Blows has stacked any speed. Do NOT chase past one Quickdraw charge: her Q hands her speed on every spell hit and she'll kite you under tower while the DOT ticks. The smoke's sight cut zones her off the wave; it never makes anything miss.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 her W move speed and Swirlseed poke compound faster than your True Grit stats matter — stacked armor does nothing against her magic Dream Dust DOT. Level 6 is your only real kill window: if she lands Swirlseed on you or commits a W bounce into range, fire Collateral Damage to burst her before her move speed carries her out of the cone, because your R is the only tool that out-damages her kite. Outside that one R window, accept you cannot pin her — your two-shell magazine forces reloads and she punishes every one with Dream Dust ticks. Trade only when R is up and she has overextended.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 her stacked speed and Swirlseed poke compound faster than your stats matter. Quickdraw's magic resist does blunt the DOT — what it cannot touch is the true damage on the outer edge of Blooming Blows, so never eat the rim of her Q. Level 6 is your only real kill window: Swirlseed is a flat 12 seconds, so the moment she throws it and misses, fire Collateral Damage before her speed carries her out of the cone. Outside that window you cannot pin her — the two-shell magazine forces reloads and she punishes every one. Trade only when your R is up.

edits.before: This is where the 37.5% shows: a fed Lillia lands R (Lilting Lullaby), the sleep plus a full Dream Dust + combo deletes you before you wake, and her Lvl 11/16 W upgrades make her literally uncatchable for your point-blank range. Your True Grit armor is dead weight against percent-irrelevant magic damage. Your only path is to have ended off an early skirmish lead and your Level 6 R window — roam, skirmish, and take objectives as a mobile carry. In a teamfight against a scaled Lillia you lose the 1v1 every time, so never face-check her sleep and let your team eat the R first.
edits.after: This is where the 37.5% shows: a fed Lillia lands R (Lilting Lullaby) — it only takes hold on targets already carrying Dream Dust, so every poke she landed was the setup — and the sleep plus a full combo deletes you before you wake. Her stacked move speed makes her uncatchable at point-blank range. Your only path is to have ended off an early skirmish lead and your Level 6 R window: roam, skirmish, take objectives as a mobile carry. You lose the 1v1 every time against a scaled Lillia, so never face-check her and let your team eat the R first.

notes: 'Blooming Blast' is a fabricated ability name that appeared six times and, worse, carried a mechanic that belongs to a different slot — Lillia's stacking move speed is the passive half of Blooming Blows (Q), not her W (Watch Out! Eep!, which is just a damage zone). Second fabrication: End of the Line was said to slow on detonation in three places. It does not; Riot's text is a shell that detonates after 1 second or on terrain. packet.suspectNames flags 'Use Smoke Screen' as a probable wrong name — false positive.
